title: Precision and accuracy
caption: Precise: someone else could build it without a single question. Accurate: the result matches the intent and solves the actual problem. You need both.

missing-requirements-show-up-as-wrong-ou.header: Missing requirements show up as wrong output
missing-requirements-show-up-as-wrong-ou.description: in 55 historic aerospace software incidents, 85% produced wrong output instead of stopping, only 16% were errors of traditional programming, and 40% came from absent code, meaning missing requirements or unanticipated situations [1].

precision.title: Precision
precision.script: Start with precision. A document is precise when someone else could execute it without asking you a single question. Nothing is left to guess.

accuracy.title: Accuracy
accuracy.script: Accuracy is a different thing: the result matches what you intended and solves the actual problem. Picture a dartboard: precision is darts landing close together, accuracy is darts landing on the bull. A document can be precise and not accurate, and then you have the ten wrong swings, built faster and with great care.

art-not-a-science.title: Art, not a science
art-not-a-science.script: Now, honesty about the craft. Writing a good requirement is an art, not a science. You only know whether it was precise and accurate after you have tried it, and that is why this Section sits where it does.
